name: FOXO4-DRI
used_for: A synthetic D-retro-inverso peptide designed to disrupt the FOXO4-p53 interaction so that senescent cells undergo apoptosis (a senolytic). It is sold online as an anti-aging research peptide. Data are from cells and mice only, including a rodent study in which clearing senescent cells worsened pulmonary hypertension, and no registered human trial was found. It is not an approved drug.

entries.text: Animal study only, not human data: in a 2020 study in naturally aged male mice (20 to 24 months), FOXO4-DRI was given at 5 mg/kg by intraperitoneal injection every other day for three administrations.

internet_entries.text: A peptide reference site that lists vendors says the research community uses 3 to 25 mg per injection, that this is highly variable, and that no established human dose exists.
internet_entries.population: As described by the source, not a study population

administration_guidance.text: A peptide guide site (peptidedosingprotocols.com, which carries affiliate links to sellers) says animal studies used injection by the intraperitoneal or intravenous route, that subcutaneous use appears only in community reports and is untested in humans, and that dry powder is stored at -20 C while mixed solution is kept at 2 to 8 C and used within a short window.
administration_guidance.label: internet

side_effects.text: A peptide guide site (peptidedosingprotocols.com, with affiliate links) says no human side effects are documented because the peptide has not been tested in people, and lists theoretical concerns including unintended cell death, immune burden from clearing dead cells, impaired wound healing and injection-site irritation.
side_effects.label: internet

side_effects.text: A rodent study found that eliminating senescent cells, including with FOXO4-DRI, promoted development and progression of pulmonary hypertension in mice and rats (animal study).
side_effects.label: research

internet_claims.claim: A peptide guide site (peptidedosingprotocols.com, with affiliate links) describes FOXO4-DRI as a senolytic that frees p53 to trigger death of senescent cells, and states that all data come from mouse and cell work with no registered human trials.

research.summary: Original description (Cell) of the FOXO4 peptide that disrupts FOXO4-p53 binding, tested in senescent cells and in mice.
research.finding: In senescent cells it caused p53 nuclear exclusion and apoptosis, and in mice it countered doxorubicin toxicity and improved fitness, fur density and renal function in fast-aging and naturally aged animals. Cell and mouse data.

research.summary: Mouse study (Aging (Albany NY)) of FOXO4-DRI in senescent Leydig cells and naturally aged mice.
research.finding: FOXO4-DRI induced apoptosis of senescent Leydig cells and alleviated age-related testosterone insufficiency in aged mice. Animal data only.

research.summary: Cell-culture study (Front Bioeng Biotechnol) in expanded human chondrocytes.
research.finding: FOXO4-DRI removed more than half of the cells at later passage and lowered senescence markers but did not improve cartilage-forming potential. Cell data only.

research.summary: Study (Circulation) of senescent cells in patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension and in rodent models, using several methods of clearing senescent cells including FOXO4-DRI.
research.finding: Senescent cell clearance promoted pulmonary hypertension development and progression in rodents, a safety signal for senolytic approaches. Animal data.

research.summary: Structural biology study (Nat Commun) using NMR of FOXO4, p53 and FOXO4-DRI.
research.finding: FOXO4-DRI binds the disordered p53 transactivation domain, which explains its mechanism. Laboratory data only.

dose.summary: No human dose exists. Mice got 5 mg/kg by injection into the belly cavity. Online sources describe anything from 250 micrograms to 25 mg per injection, with none of it tested in people.

items.text: Animal study only, not human data: aged male mice (20 to 24 months) received 5 mg/kg by intraperitoneal injection (into the belly cavity) every other day for three doses.

mechanism.summary: Designed to block the FOXO4 and p53 partnership inside aged (senescent) cells so they self-destruct. This was shown in cells and mice only, not in people.

items.text: In senescent cells the peptide caused p53 to leave the nucleus and triggered cell death (apoptosis). Cell and mouse data, from the 2017 Cell paper.
items.label: research

items.text: Structural lab work (NMR) found that FOXO4-DRI binds the disordered p53 activation region, which explains how it works. Laboratory data only.
items.label: research

items.text: Wikipedia describes FOXO4-DRI as a synthetic all-D-amino-acid retro-inverso peptide that blocks FOXO4, which frees p53 to trigger death of senescent cells while sparing healthy cells. The article cites only preclinical work.
items.label: internet

best_documented_effect.summary: No human data exist. In aged mice it improved fitness, fur density, kidney function and testosterone production. In human cartilage cells it cleared cells but did not improve cartilage quality.

items.text: Mouse results: in fast-aging and naturally aged mice it improved fitness, fur density and kidney function, and countered doxorubicin toxicity. No human trial exists.
items.label: research

items.text: In naturally aged mice it raised testosterone output by clearing senescent Leydig (testis) cells. Animal data only.
items.label: research

items.text: In human cartilage cells grown in a dish it removed more than half the cells at later passage but did not improve cartilage-forming potential.
items.label: research

side_effect_groups.title: No human data
side_effect_groups.summary: FOXO4-DRI has never been tested in people, so no human side effects are documented. Seller-linked sites list theoretical concerns only.

side_effect_groups.title: In animals
side_effect_groups.summary: In rodents, clearing senescent cells, including with FOXO4-DRI, worsened pulmonary hypertension (high blood pressure in the lung arteries). This is a safety signal and is not human data.

items.text: A rodent study found that eliminating senescent cells, including with FOXO4-DRI, promoted development and progression of pulmonary hypertension in mice and rats (animal study).
items.label: research

side_effect_groups.title: Online reports
side_effect_groups.summary: One seller-linked site lists injection-site burning or itching, fatigue, muscle soreness and nausea, while also saying human safety data are limited. No source for these was given.

items.text: Peptibase, a site that links to sellers, says side effects are injection site reactions (burning, itching), fatigue, muscle soreness and nausea, that it is generally well tolerated in animal studies, and that human safety data are limited.
